note: MATERIAL had no descriptions anywhere in the catalog, so these set the register: treat each substance as real, give it one working property and one consequence of that property. Written to be useful to a smith and to an image model at the same time.

entries.title: Adamantium
entries.description: Does not bend, does not break, does not care. Working it at all requires a tool that was never supposed to exist.

entries.title: Amberlight
entries.description: Fossilised light, set solid. Warm in the hand, and whatever was caught inside is still faintly moving.

entries.title: Angelite
entries.description: Pale blue and unnervingly calm. Smiths report the whole workshop goes quiet while it is on the bench.

entries.title: Ashglass
entries.description: Fused from what a fire left behind. Holds an edge and a grudge in roughly equal measure.

entries.title: Bloodstone
entries.description: Dark green shot through with red. Old medicine swore by it; old soldiers carried it regardless of the medicine.

entries.title: Cloudstone
entries.description: Weighs almost nothing and holds its shape anyway. Falls slower than it should, which unsettles everyone the first time.

entries.title: Cryolite
entries.description: Melts at a temperature that makes no sense for a stone, and takes whatever it was packed with down alongside it.

entries.title: Dreamcloth
entries.description: Woven by someone while asleep. The pattern is never twice the same and nobody has photographed it successfully.

entries.title: Fulgurite
entries.description: Sand struck by lightning and frozen mid-decision. Hollow, branching, and far too fragile for what made it.

entries.title: Glowstone
entries.description: Gives off a steady light with no source anyone can locate. Does not dim, does not warm, does not explain.

entries.title: Hexstone
entries.description: Six-sided all the way through, however it is broken. Carvers find this convenient and faintly rude.

entries.title: Ironwood
entries.description: Blunts the saw and sinks in water. Every joint cut from it outlasts the person who cut it.

entries.title: Moonstone
entries.description: Sheens blue when turned, and only when turned. Sits inert on a shelf, which is precisely why it is worn instead.

entries.title: Mythril
entries.description: Light enough to forget you are wearing it, strong enough that forgetting is safe. Ruinously scarce for exactly that reason.

entries.title: Obsidian
entries.description: Volcanic glass with an edge finer than steel and no patience whatsoever for being dropped.

entries.title: Runestone
entries.description: Takes a carved mark and keeps it working long after the carver stopped. Chips badly if the mark was wrong.

entries.title: Shadewood
entries.description: Grew somewhere the light never reached. Dark the whole way through and noticeably cool to the touch.

entries.title: Starsteel
entries.description: Fell before it was ever forged. Holds a temper nothing terrestrial can match and rings at a pitch nobody enjoys.

entries.title: Stormglass
entries.description: Clouds over before the weather arrives, reliably enough that sailors trusted it over the sky itself.

entries.title: Tanglewood
entries.description: Grain running in every direction at once. Impossible to split cleanly and correspondingly difficult to break.

entries.title: Timeglass
entries.description: Anything seen through it is running slightly behind. Useful for study and genuinely dangerous for aiming.

entries.title: Titanite
entries.description: Wedge-shaped crystals with more fire than a diamond and considerably less sense about being struck.

entries.title: Voidsteel
entries.description: Absorbs light and returns none of it. Edges made from this are hard to see and consequently hard to avoid.

entries.title: Aether Silk
entries.description: Spun from the medium itself. Registers nothing on the scale and still catches on a breeze.

entries.title: Ancient Marble
entries.description: Quarried before anybody kept records. Takes a polish that modern stone simply will not hold.

entries.title: Arcane Silver
entries.description: Tarnishes toward a pattern rather than a stain. Jewellers still argue about whether that counts as damage.

entries.title: Astral Ore
entries.description: Mined from something that was never a planet. Hums faintly whenever two pieces are brought near each other.

entries.title: Bio-metal
entries.description: Grows rather than being cast, and closes a scratch given a week and something to eat.

entries.title: Blaze Ore
entries.description: Warm out of the ground and warmer once worked. Storage is a genuine engineering problem rather than a precaution.

entries.title: Bone Glass
entries.description: Fired from ash and calcium into something translucent. Beautiful, and everybody knows exactly what it was.

entries.title: Charged Crystal
entries.description: Holds a current indefinitely and releases all of it the moment it cracks. Anyone experienced handles it with tongs.

entries.title: Chimeric Thread
entries.description: Three fibres that should not spin together, spun together. The resulting cloth behaves like none of the three.

entries.title: Chrono Dust
entries.description: Settles slower than it falls. A pinch in an hourglass makes the hour noticeably longer for everyone in the room.

entries.title: Cosmic Ice
entries.description: Never melted because it never once got the chance. Colder than ice has any business being, and it does not sweat.

entries.title: Crimson Coral
entries.description: Grown slowly in deep water and red the whole way through. Cutting it ends the growth permanently.

entries.title: Cryo Iron
entries.description: Stays below freezing inside a furnace. Smiths work it with heated tools, backwards from every instinct they have.

entries.title: Cursed Iron
entries.description: Perfectly ordinary metal that keeps arriving in the wrong hands at the worst hour. The metallurgy checks out completely.

entries.title: Cursed Velvet
entries.description: Rich, heavy, and warm in a room that is not. Nobody who owns a bolt can recall buying it.

entries.title: Dark Matter Thread
entries.description: Has mass and declines to interact with anything else. Sewing it requires a needle that also declines.

entries.title: Demonic Bone
entries.description: Denser than it looks and still faintly warm. Carves beautifully. Carvers report unusual dreams afterward.

entries.title: Dragon Scale
entries.description: Overlaps into armor that shrugs off flame because it grew up in flame. Each plate outlasts the smith who set it.

entries.title: Dragonbone Porcelain
entries.description: Ground bone fired into something you can read a page through. Fragile in the hand and unbreakable in reputation.

entries.title: Echo Crystal
entries.description: Returns a sound minutes after receiving it. Rooms lined with the stuff get used for confession and for interrogation.

entries.title: Eclipse Stone
entries.description: Dark with a bright rim that does not move regardless of the light. Every polisher has tried to remove it.

entries.title: Eldritch Thread
entries.description: Measures differently depending on when it is measured. Tailors work fast and pointedly do not check twice.

entries.title: Enchanted Bark
entries.description: Peeled without harming the tree, which carries on producing it. The arrangement predates the forest's current shape.

entries.title: Ethereal Mist
entries.description: Treated as a material by people who insist that it is one. Holds a shape for exactly as long as it is watched.

entries.title: Fire Opal
entries.description: Orange and alive with internal light. Cracks if it dries out, so it has to be worn rather than stored.

entries.title: Frostbite Alloy
entries.description: Pulls heat out of whatever touches it. Excellent for blades, poor for handles, and fatal for gloves.

entries.title: Galactic Granite
entries.description: Speckled the way a night sky is, and the speckles are not minerals. Nobody has yet agreed what they are.

entries.title: Ghost Iron
entries.description: Weighs correctly and passes straight through cloth. Blacksmiths who work it tend to stop taking commissions.

entries.title: Glacial Shard
entries.description: Compressed over centuries into something harder than rock. Still ice, and still holding air from the year it formed.

entries.title: Heavensteel
entries.description: Forged somewhere with better light. Takes an edge that will not dull and reflects more than is actually in the room.

entries.title: Hollow Steel
entries.description: Full strength at a third of the weight, because most of it is deliberate absence. Rings like a bell when struck.

entries.title: Infernal Brimstone
entries.description: Yellow, acrid, and never entirely cool. Useful, and every single use smells the same afterward.

entries.title: Liquid Gold
entries.description: Stays liquid at room temperature and stays gold throughout. Kept in glass, poured for effect, never actually spent.

entries.title: Living Wood
entries.description: Cut and still growing. A door made from it will want trimming every spring for the rest of its life.

entries.title: Lunar Resin
entries.description: Hardens only in darkness. Workshops that use it have no windows and no explanation ready for visitors.

entries.title: Magic-infused Clay
entries.description: Takes a shape and remembers it. Fired or not, it will return to that shape given long enough alone.

entries.title: Mirror Alloy
entries.description: Polishes to a reflection with no distortion at any angle. The absence of distortion is the part people find unsettling.

entries.title: Molten Core
entries.description: Never solidifies. Kept in containment, used sparingly, and blamed for most workshop fires in the district.

entries.title: Moonlit Granite
entries.description: Grey by day and faintly luminous after dark, which makes it standard for anything meant to be found at night.

entries.title: Nano-carbon
entries.description: A lattice engineered a molecule at a time. Stronger than steel, thinner than paper, and impossible to repair in the field.

entries.title: Nebula Thread
entries.description: Dyed by something enormous and very far away. Every bolt is unique and no two dyers can match one.

entries.title: Nether Ore
entries.description: Comes up from below the levels anybody maps. Smelts reluctantly and stains the crucible permanently.

entries.title: Oblivion Alloy
entries.description: Objects made from it are difficult to remember afterward. Inventories get kept in duplicate for that reason alone.

entries.title: Phantom Glass
entries.description: Transparent from one side and simply absent from the other. Windows of it have caused several arguments about direction.

entries.title: Phoenix Feather
entries.description: Survives its own burning and comes out weighing the same. Quills cut from it never once need trimming.

entries.title: Plasma Alloy
entries.description: Metal held just short of becoming something else. Conducts everything and tolerates almost nothing.

entries.title: Platinum Filigree
entries.description: Drawn to a thread and worked into patterns finer than the eye resolves. The work gets measured in months.

entries.title: Prismarine Shard
entries.description: Sea-green and shifting, wet even when dry. Underwater construction depends on it because nothing else behaves the same.

entries.title: Prismatic Ore
entries.description: Splits every light that enters into its parts. Mining it by lamp is reportedly overwhelming.

entries.title: Pulse Metal
entries.description: Expands and contracts on a slow rhythm. Any fitting made from it has to be designed around the beat.

entries.title: Pyroclastic Rock
entries.description: Cooled from a cloud that outran everything in its path. Porous, light, and still carrying the shape of that hurry.

entries.title: Quantum Fiber
entries.description: Measurably in two places until examined. Rope made from it is reliable only while nobody watches the far end.

entries.title: Radiant Amber
entries.description: Fossil resin that kept the light along with the insect. Warms the hand and lights a small room unaided.

entries.title: Radiant Silk
entries.description: Woven fine enough to scatter light forward. Worn by people who want to be seen and cannot say so aloud.

entries.title: Shadow Oak
entries.description: Timber from trees grown under permanent overcast. Dense, dark, and it takes a stain the way nothing else does.

entries.title: Shadow Weave
entries.description: Cloth that reads as a gap rather than a garment. Tailors work it by touch, because looking does not help.

entries.title: Shimmer Cloth
entries.description: Changes colour with the angle and never settles on one. Photographs badly, which has only ever increased demand.

entries.title: Solar Flame
entries.description: Captured at the source and still burning. Nothing else gives that light and nothing else is as difficult to insure.

entries.title: Solar Glass
entries.description: Takes light in all day and gives it back all night, on a curve nobody has managed to flatten.

entries.title: Soul Sand
entries.description: Slows anything crossing it, sound included. Walking on it takes twice as long and feels considerably longer than that.

entries.title: Specter Silk
entries.description: Spun by something nobody has ever seen at work. Weighs nothing and holds a knot indefinitely.

entries.title: Spectral Quartz
entries.description: Clear until it is turned, at which point it briefly shows something that was in the room earlier.

entries.title: Spire Crystal
entries.description: Grows upward in single columns and refuses to branch. Architects have built whole districts on that reliability.

entries.title: Starfire Iron
entries.description: Retains the heat of its arrival and has not cooled since. Forges get built around a single ingot.

entries.title: Starfruit Fiber
entries.description: Stripped from a plant that only sets fruit under clear skies. Strong, faintly sweet, and seasonal in a way industry hates.

entries.title: Starlight Powder
entries.description: Ground from something that fell. A pinch lights a page, a spoonful lights a hall, and neither can be put out.

entries.title: Storm Weave
entries.description: Cloth carrying a static charge it never loses. Raises hair across the room and keeps the wearer perfectly dry.

entries.title: Temporal Resin
entries.description: Sets at its own pace and disregards the clock entirely. A joint sealed with it may cure in an hour or in a decade.

entries.title: Thunderstone
entries.description: Cracked open, it discharges once and is ordinary ever after. Miners treat it as a single-use decision.

entries.title: Tidal Pearl
entries.description: Grows on a lunar cycle and bands accordingly. Reading the bands gives you the year it started.

entries.title: Venom Glass
entries.description: Poured with the toxin still in it. Beautiful, edged, and never used for drinking vessels by anyone informed.

entries.title: Void Crystal
entries.description: Clear, and containing nothing at all, aggressively. Instruments near it read low across the board.

entries.title: Vortex Gem
entries.description: The inclusion inside is turning and has not stopped. Everyone who has watched it for long advises against doing so.

entries.title: Warped Stone
entries.description: Refuses to sit level on any surface. Masons compensate by building the entire wall to its opinion.

entries.title: Warped Velvet
entries.description: The nap runs in directions that change while unobserved. Upholsterers charge extra and explain why at length.

entries.title: Whisperwood
entries.description: Carries sound along the grain for a considerable distance. Walls built from it are never used for private rooms.
